dataset.description:
The research objective is to develop a methodology for monitoring ship power systems- diesel engines, based on the method of non-destructive testing and diagnostics. The following tasks will be carried out:
1. Analysis of the main kinds and the nature of operational defects of engines. Identification of monitoring objects. Analysis of the existing approaches to predicting engine life cycles.
2. Analysis and evaluation of the effectiveness of existing engine monitoring systems and condition based on maintenance of engines. Analysis of the existing approaches to assess engine reliability and their maintenance cycle predictions;
3. Evaluation of test possibility of ship engines; selection and justification of diagnostic methods and corresponding informative parameters. Preparation and submission of project proposal to Horizon Europe call for proposals;
4. Development of diagnostic models and diagnostic algorithms of engines, their systems, components and parts. Development of monitoring methodology, experimental studies and diagnostic tests for engines and their systems. Preparation of two publications together with collaboration scientist from Texas A&M University

distribution.title: The use of acoustic emission (AE) as a diagnostic tool for diesel engine fuel systems is of scientific and practical interest. The use of AE as a diagnostic tool, if successful, can significantly expand the diagnostic capabilities of diesel engine fuel and valve systems. Diagnostics of diesel fuel equipment, its preventative maintenance, and repair of the engine system (injection pump and injectors) can identify and resolve issues related to excessive fuel consumption and unstable engine operation.
